title: The node's knowledge graph: agent memory on LightRAG
description: The node's agents keep what they learn and find it again by meaning. Knowledge outlives the conversation, and an agent reads a short extract instead of whole files.
keywords: knowledge graph, LightRAG, agent memory, graph RAG, Fractera node

blocks.title: Your agents stop forgetting what they learned
blocks.description: The graph keeps the knowledge of every element of your node: what was studied, how it connects and where it came from. Any agent finds what it needs with one question instead of rereading old files and conversations.

blocks.title: Without a shared memory every conversation starts from zero

blocks.text: An agent studied someone else's site, worked out how its cart works and explained it all to you. The conversation closed and the finding was gone. A week later another agent does the same work again, and you pay for the tokens again.

children.text: What an agent finds goes into the graph and survives the end of the conversation, a restart of the node and a change of agent.
Search by meaning and by links
Ask in plain words: the graph finds the text that matches and everything connected to it, down to an item of your product quiz.
An agent gets a short extract made for its question and does not reread reports hundreds of megabytes long.
One graph for the whole node
What one element gathers is there for all the others at once.

blocks.text: Picture a map where the towns are things and the roads are the links between them. A site, its search, the request address that search uses and the item of your quiz that grew out of it are points on that map, joined by labelled lines. The graph remembers both the points and the roads between them.

steps.title: An agent saves
steps.text: An element hands the graph what it learned: the things, the links between them and a short text saying where it came from.

steps.title: The graph connects
steps.text: New knowledge settles next to what is already known, and the same thing found in different analyses becomes one point.

steps.title: Any agent asks
steps.text: For a question in plain words the graph returns a short context: the right things, their links and the source.

items.label: model calls to save knowledge that is already structured
embedding to find the answer to a question
tokens of things and of links in an answer, at most

blocks.text: Embeddings use the OpenAI key of your node. In the graph search modes a question costs one more short model call that picks out its keywords. The limits are defaults and can be changed.

The graph runs inside the node on your computer, and its data sits in the node's folder. Elements read it and add to it through the element's doors with the node's key. When you need to, you can connect your own tools to the same doors.

children.text: An agent works out how a feature of someone else's site is built and writes into the graph the site, the feature, the requests behind it and the quiz item that grew out of it. The finding does not vanish with the conversation.
Collections of skills, MCP servers and any set where it matters not only what is in it but how one thing relates to another. The graph keeps them in order and finds what you need by meaning.
The memory of all the node's agents

Everything that happened in the agents' lives in one place: what happened and when, which element, node and partner it involves, which event was the cause and which the effect. Together it gives the whole picture of your project.

items.q: Do I need to install anything?
items.a: No. The element installs Python and LightRAG into its own folder, and nothing goes into the system.
In the node's folder on your computer. The graph lives in the memory of its process, and the files on disk are its copy.

items.q: Can I connect to the graph from outside?
items.a: Yes. Today the node's elements use the graph through its doors with the node's key. You can connect your own tools to the same doors.
An open-source library for search over a knowledge graph, from the LightRAG Team under the MIT license. The node's graph is built on it.

items.q: What if the graph gets very large?
items.a: The built-in storage is enough for the knowledge of one node. A graph of millions of things needs a database server, and this element does not set one up.

items.text: Hello. I am opening a hair salon called «Strand». I heard a website can now be made completely automatically?
Hello, Anna! This is the Fractera agent. That is right — it takes a couple of simple steps.
Install Claude Code — one line in a terminal, from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup. Working with AI needs a subscription — the Pro plan at $20 a month will do, and it includes Claude Code.
Installed and signed in. What next?
Your project will live on GitHub. Create a free account there, open https://github.com/fractera/agi and press Fork — all the project files land in your GitHub. Copy the address of your copy.
Done, copied it.

Make an empty folder for the project, open a terminal in it and run claude. Paste the link and write: «launch this». The agent reads the instructions, in a few minutes brings up your own server on this computer and puts it on the internet.
It installed everything and gave me the address on the internet right away: https://strand-7f3k.trycloudflare.com

Great, your project is running! Right now your own computer is the server. This address is temporary — your own domain will make it permanent, and with it the salon pages stay open at all times, even while the computer is off. The services — booking, the client base, the assistant — need the computer switched on. That is enough to start with, and when you need it we will move you to a real server (VPS). You can close this window: from here on your own agent, the lead orchestrator agent, takes over. Most of the time you will talk to it in Telegram, and it carries out your commands.
The «Strand» project is handed over to the lead orchestrator agent on your server.
Hi! Please make a website for my hair salon. Here is the description I prepared.
Thank you for the detailed description. I will need a little time. Meanwhile, think about which extra services you need.
How much will it cost?
It is free: we build it on your server with the Claude Code agent. You can change it as often as you like — it is a simple service, and it needs no outside solutions.
I need online booking, a client base and an assistant that answers when the salon is closed.
New project. Anna is opening «Strand», a hair salon. Assembling a team of agents.
How many stylists and which services? The booking grid depends on it.
Three stylists: haircuts, colouring, styling. Colouring takes two hours, the rest one hour.

departure.label: Departure
departure.question: I want to set off. Walk me through the whole launch, step by step.
departure.answer:
The launch, step by step:
1. Install Claude Code — one line in a terminal, from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup — and take the Pro plan at $20 a month: Claude Code is included.
2. Create a free GitHub account, open https://github.com/fractera/agi, press Fork and copy the address of your copy.
3. Make an empty folder for the project, open a terminal in it, run claude, paste the link and write «launch this».
4. The agent installs the node, checks that it works on your computer and puts it on the internet right away at a temporary Cloudflare address.
5. From then on your own lead orchestrator agent works with you, mostly in Telegram.
6. Later you buy your own domain and connect it on the node page «Domain and hosting → Domain activation».
Start now: open https://github.com/fractera/agi and press Fork.

transfer.label: Transfers en route
transfer.question: What transfers are there en route? How does the project grow and get new capabilities?
transfer.answer: The project grows by elements: the site, sign-in, data, design, blocks and whatever you add are separate elements, each with its own agent. A new element is born from the template with «Create AGI ITEM» on your node, and new features you order from the lead orchestrator agent in the chat or in Telegram.

answers: The Fractera node itself is open and free. You pay only for Claude Pro — $20 a month, Claude Code included — and, if you want, for your own domain at a registrar. The Cloudflare tunnel and the copy of your pages run on the free plan, and your computer is the server; a rented server (VPS) comes later, only if you want it.
Texts, photos, documents and the description of your business you simply hand to the agent in the chat. All the data lives on your own computer.
People see the site in every language you choose. Search engines get English and your default language; you open the other languages to them yourself, one by one.
The code is open and lives with you: if Fractera disappeared tomorrow, nothing of yours would break. You can cancel the Claude subscription with Anthropic at any time.
A computer, Claude Code on the Pro plan and a free GitHub account. For a permanent address: your own domain and a free Cloudflare account.

The agents of your elements work in the terminal and in Telegram, a watchdog restarts the site by itself, and the node starts on its own when the computer is switched on. With your own domain the public pages stay visible even while the computer is off.
